A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DAREx study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite changes in pagination and formatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model pruning experiments, controlled two-layer network experiments, and supplementary regularization, activation, and efficiency analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds training-dynamics experiments, CIFAR-100 and 13B-model evaluations, and AdamR-L2 results with LoRA.

M1.justification: DAREx-q's rescaling variants, AdamR-L1/L2 updates, and Algorithms 1–3 remain unchanged. The additional ViT, 13B-model, and regularized LoRA evaluations apply existing methods without specifying a new update rule or pruning component.

E1.justification: Appendix G.1 adds CIFAR-100 object classification. Vision was already represented by the CIFAR-10 pretraining and digit-classification experiment in Appendix B, so this extends existing coverage. The 13B evaluation retains MetaMath/GSM8K, and the additional LoRA experiment retains the four language-understanding tasks.

E2.justification: Appendix F introduces explicit training-loss comparisons between AdamR's delta decay and vanilla weight decay. The existing DARE, random-drop, MP, WANDA, Diff, and Diff-struct comparisons are retained; the new benchmark evaluations do not introduce additional pruning baselines.

E3.justification: New experiments add ViT and 13B configurations, AdamR-regularized LoRA evaluation at p=0.99, and BERT training-loss comparisons at moderate and 1e-2 regularization strengths. Existing evaluation metrics and Appendix C.2 settings remain unchanged; these are additional settings, not documented reruns of the original comparisons.

E4.justification: Appendix F and Figures 11–12 add a focused analysis of convergence and sensitivity to stronger regularization. Appendix G.3 compares LoRA pruning with and without AdamR-L2. Earlier pruning-rate, normalization, structured-pruning, and activation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Section 5.1 retains averages and standard deviations over four independent runs. Existing uncertainty reporting is unchanged, and the new figures and Tables 15–16 introduce no additional run-count, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-test reporting.

E6.justification: Existing results are retained, while Appendices F–G substantially expand the reported evidence. At p=0.99, Table 15 adds CIFAR-100 scores of 32.74 for DARE, 84.11 for DAREx-q, and 83.84 for DAREx-L2; MetaMath-13B scores are 0.00 versus 44.73 for DARE and DAREx-q. Table 16 adds LoRA results, and Figures 11–12 add training-loss findings. These are new comparisons, not improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: Appendix E.1 adds a central-limit-theorem argument claiming tight dependence on p for Theorem 3.1. The theorem and existing derivations remain unchanged. The added argument contains variance and normalization inconsistencies, and the new E.1.1 'Lower bound' heading has no separate proof beneath it.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: explaining DARE's failure modes, proposing DAREx-q and AdamR, and guiding selection of pruning methods. The additional experiments support these contributions without redefining the main claims.

C2.justification: Appendix F interprets the new curves as evidence that delta decay preserves convergence while tolerating stronger regularization. Appendix G extends the applicability discussion to ViTs and larger models, while explicitly noting that resource constraints prevented 13B fine-tuning. Sections 3.2 and 4.1 also qualify the predicted growth rate with 'at most.'

D1.justification: New material identifies ImageNet-21k pretraining for the ViT and specifies regularization strengths for the training-dynamics experiments. Existing hardware, encoder training settings, decoding settings, algorithms, and code-access information remain unchanged. The added experiments receive only limited configuration detail.

R1.justification: v2 adds Dosovitskiy (2020) and Ridnik et al. (2021) references for ViT and ImageNet-21k. The substantive positioning relative to DARE, importance-based pruning, parameter-efficient tuning, and sparse fine-tuning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: There are limited wording, affiliation, and acknowledgment edits. The method-selection explanation moves from Section 6 to Appendix C.3, and the main-text broader-impact summary becomes an appendix pointer. Appendices F–G are added, but most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: The document adopts the ICLR conference layout throughout, changing the title block, headers, section typography, spacing, and float placement. Existing figures and tables are redistributed, including separating Figures 6 and 7 onto different pages. Figures 11–12 and Tables 15–16 are new; the earlier displays largely retain their content.

improvement.justification: Appendices F–G usefully strengthen validation through training-stability checks, a practical ViT evaluation, a 13B-model test, and AdamR with LoRA. These provide incremental support beyond v1's already extensive experiments. The benefit is limited by sparse implementation and uncertainty reporting for the additions, while the new tightness argument introduces mathematical inconsistencies rather than a complete rigorous justification.
